references.text: The psalmist complains that friends and acquaintances keep their distance in times of suffering: "My friends and my companions stand aloof from my plague" (Ps 38:12). This is a prophetic parallel to the fact that Jesus' acquaintances stood at a distance watching his suffering.
The psalmist says: "You have put my friends far away from me" (Ps 88:9). This reflects the situation at the cross where Jesus' acquaintances stood far off.

"You have put friend and companion far away from me" (Ps 88:19). Another psalm passage that speaks of close friends distancing themselves in times of trouble, just as Jesus' acquaintances stood at a distance during the crucifixion.

Matthew's parallel account tells us that many women who had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him were standing there watching from a distance (Matt 27:55-56). This is the closest parallel to Luke's account.

Mark also mentions women who watched from a distance, identifying some of them by name, including Mary Magdalene, Mary (the mother of James and Joses), and Salome, who had followed him from Galilee (Mk 15:40-41).

John tells us that Jesus' mother, her sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene stood near the cross (Jn 19:25-27). While Luke describes them standing at a distance, John places some of the women close to the cross.
Luke mentions earlier that a group of women followed Jesus from Galilee and served him with their possessions (Lk 8:2-3). These are the same women who now stood by the cross and witnessed his death.
Earlier on the way to Golgotha, Jesus addressed the women of Jerusalem who were following him and weeping (Lk 23:27-28). Women were thus present both along the way and at the crucifixion itself.

The same women who had followed Jesus from Galilee followed after and saw the tomb where his body was laid, then went home to prepare spices and ointments (Lk 23:55-56). These are the same witnesses who stood at a distance watching the crucifixion.
After the ascension, the apostles and some women gathered for prayer (Acts 1:11-14). The women who had been faithful witnesses at the cross were also present in the first church.
